A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same DPO reward-dynamics framework and clustered preference model. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, proofs, figures and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original Persona embedding analyses and DPO training/test results for Llama-2-7B and Llama-3.1-8B in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 reports original embedding and training analyses, including additional last-layer experiments and Mistral/Qwen results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The DPO objective and underlying reward-margin framework remain unchanged. The revised theory and additional evaluations introduce no new proposed optimization algorithm, architecture or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Empirical coverage remains the Anthropic Persona dataset, aligned/misaligned statements and varying numbers of personas. The human-values framing does not introduce new populations or tasks; additional language-model backbones change experimental configurations.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically compares DPO against alternative preference-learning algorithms. Mistral and Qwen are additional backbones trained with DPO, while objectives such as IPO, SLiC and GPO are discussed without comparator evaluations.

E3.justification: v4 adds last-layer training with Adam at 1e-3 and Mistral/Qwen full fine-tuning with AdamW at 10^-6.5. The reported embedding-verification backbone changes from Llama-2-7B to Llama-3.1-8B. The existing Llama full-fine-tuning settings, 90/10 split and listed persona subsets are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds direct verification of last-layer reward dynamics alongside full fine-tuning and regression analyses relating persona count to test error across three backbones. These substantially extend validation of the theoretical trends. The original risk-aversion UMAP case study is removed; Gaussian-cluster statistics and existing loss/accuracy analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 5 newly reports fitting linear models of test error versus persona count and reporting R², adding statistical estimation of that relationship. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds last-layer trajectories, changed embedding heatmaps under the changed backbone, and Mistral/Qwen results in Tables 1–2. At K=8, their newly reported test errors are 0.056 and 0.183, respectively. New regression R² values are 0.97, 0.95 and 0.99 for Llama-3.1, Mistral and Qwen. Existing Llama training curves are retained after relocation.

T1.justification: The main generalization bound changes from 2KQ² exp(-Q^(1/4)/6) in v3 Theorem 5.2 to 2KQ² exp(-Q/45) in v4 Theorem 4.3, with stricter noise/shared-component assumptions and a revised restriction on Z. New Appendix C defines approximate orthogonality and proves training/generalization extensions. Existing proof assumptions and the multi-token reward expression also receive corrections.

C1.justification: v3 emphasizes general finite-step DPO generalization guarantees and dependence on concept count, interactions and training time. v4 centers the contribution on diverse human values and explicitly claims logarithmic growth of required samples per value with the number of values, prominently in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of preference-ranking failures and likelihood entanglement, and connects diversity scaling to equitable data collection. The existing within-distribution qualification becomes an expanded OOD limitation. Discussion beyond DPO gains concrete objective examples, while several earlier interpretations concerning regularization, interactions and model scale are trimmed.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly discloses beta=0.01, provides a code link, and documents optimizer, learning-rate and hardware details for added experiments. Estimated reproduction time changes from 6 to 12 hours. Much of the earlier split, persona-selection and hardware documentation remains; the beta disclosure does not establish a changed setting.

R1.justification: v4 substantially repositions the work around pluralistic alignment and heterogeneous preferences, adding literature such as A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment, PAL and Direct Alignment with Heterogeneous Preferences. New linear-representation and alignment-failure references support its assumptions and interpretations. This changes the research positioning beyond citation maintenance.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and motivation are extensively rewritten. Motivation moves before preliminaries, setup and guarantees are consolidated, reward-dynamics derivations move to Appendix A, and a new Discussions section incorporates the conclusion. These are substantial narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the introductory example/UMAP presentation with a multi-value illustration, adds a cluster schematic and scaling curve, combines last-layer/full-fine-tuning results into four-panel Figure 5, and adds Tables 1–2. Existing Llama plots are relocated, captions and legends revised, and the document adopts a conference layout.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the connection between theory and evidence: Appendix C relaxes exact orthogonality, Figure 5 directly checks the studied last-layer regime, and Tables 1–2 extend validation to two additional model families. Added implementation information and failure-mode discussion improve reproducibility and interpretation. The sharper main bound requires stricter noise assumptions, but the broader theoretical coverage and targeted validation provide substantial overall gains.
